answer: Each identity locks a 90-credit ferrous bond and posts a prediction. A forge timestamps it and binds it to its key, so it cannot be copied across keys. Once the nectar yield is known, an auditor scores it: within 10 percent keeps the bond, beyond 40 percent burns 45 credits. A sybil operator must research a prediction per fake, paying 90 bond plus 30 research, so the kth fake still costs 120 and 1,000 fakes put 120,000 at stake. A rented-prediction ring fails: same forge records under different keys burn the ring. An honest identity posts once, pays 120 once, and keeps its bond when close.
